idea-plugin.name: Keep Mac Awake
idea-plugin.description:
Keeps your Mac awake from the IDE, also with the MacBook lid closed, so a long build, a test suite or an AI agent such as Junie keeps running. The plugin controls the Keep Mac Awake menu bar app through its keepmacawake command.

The Keep Mac Awake app is required. It has a free trial and runs on any Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. Without the app, the plugin tells you what is missing and installs nothing.

  • Start (Tools | Keep Mac Awake): keeps the Mac awake for the hours you choose, 8 by default. The session ends by itself after its hours, or with Stop, and normal sleep returns. During the free trial a session lasts at most 8 hours.
  • Stop: ends the session, only when this IDE started it. A session started from the menu bar, a terminal or an agent is left running; stop it from the menu bar panel.
  • Status: whether a session runs, its time left and the free trial.
  • Keep this Mac awake while a run configuration runs (optional, off by default, in Settings | Tools | Keep Mac Awake): a run starts a timed session, and the end of the run ends it, only when the plugin started it.
  • On battery: on a MacBook running on battery, Keep Mac Awake turns Run on battery on at 20% unless you set it yourself. While it turned itself on, Start asks before a session that may run on battery, and runs start no session until you said yes. The plugin never changes the setting.

The plugin runs only /usr/local/bin/keepmacawake with status, start --hours N and stop. It makes no network connection and reads no project files. On Windows and Linux it loads, and its actions explain that it is for Macs.
